intro: Guyana is the only English-speaking country in South America and has become one of the world's fastest-growing economies thanks to oil.

chapters.title: Land of many waters
text: 'Guyana' comes from an Indigenous word meaning 'land of many waters'. Arawak, Carib and Warao peoples lived here before Europeans arrived.

chapters.title: Dutch and British rule
text: The Dutch built sugar plantations worked by enslaved Africans. Britain took over in 1814. After slavery ended, about 240,000 indentured workers came, mainly from India, shaping today's population.

highlight.title: Demerara
highlight.text: The 1823 Demerara rebellion of enslaved people helped push Britain to end slavery.

chapters.title: Independence and oil
text: Guyana became independent in 1966. Politics has often divided along ethnic lines. Huge offshore oil discoveries from 2015 transformed the economy. Venezuela claims the Essequibo region, two-thirds of Guyana's land.

keyTerms.meaning: A contract binding workers for years.
